about: Build rows (felizjueves.measured_store, #146): the host wall-clock of ONE WHOLE-MOLECULE J_p BUILD from a launch.LaunchPlan on one card -- every class's batch kernels into one J_p per bra class -- timed behind the card gate (felizjueves.gate), keyed by build_key. Its own file: a build is no MeasuredKey's Spec, and kernels.json's rows are not widened. Observations of two cards and their toolchains, NOT comparable to [JEngine]'s A100 figures, nor across vendors.

header.what: One row per timed whole-molecule J_p build (launch.launches -> test/plan_driver.py's generated driver), per card, per arm.
header.key: build_key(fixture, tau, n_batches, density_sort, arm, arch, toolchain) = '<fixture>/tau=<repr>/b=<n>/sort=<density|global>/<arm>@<arch>/<toolchain>'. fixture is test/oracle/fixtures/<fixture>.json (the molecule, basis and density); n_batches is the plan's fixed count, or 'dispatch:<input>' for a plan resolved per class by dispatch.Resolver(arch, <input>); density_sort is launch.launches' sort key (density: G * Dmax per ket; global: one global Dmax, so the order is by G alone); arm labels a same-session A/B (#147) -- 'baseline' is the plan's default, timed alone.
header.timed_region: runtime_ns / spread_ns / repeats are the MEDIAN, the INTERQUARTILE RANGE and the COUNT of `repeats` timed builds (after raw 'build:warmup' untimed ones, all in ONE process), host std::chrono::steady_clock. ONE TIMED BUILD IS, in order: (a) one device memset zeroing each bra class's J_p buffer; (b) every batch kernel of every (lp, lq) class of the plan, launched in plan order on the default stream into its bra class's J_p (fp64 atomics); (c) one device synchronize; (d) the device-to-host copy of every bra class's J_p (one blocking copy per bra class). It starts after a device synchronize, so no earlier work is inside it. raw 'build:device_median_ns' is (a)-(c) alone and 'build:readback_median_ns' is (d) alone (each the median over the same repeats); 'build:events_median_ns' is the GPU-event time from before (a) to after (b). OUTSIDE THE CLOCK: process start, reading the input file, the VRAM probe, every device allocation, and the H2D UPLOADS -- one per bra class (P zeta Ip) and one per ket class (Q eta Iq Dmax D), done ONCE per process before the first build and timed once, apart, as raw 'build:upload_ns' (a single observation, allocation included); the host-side staging that builds those buffers (Python, ao.staged); the host-side eq. 20 back-transform and J_ab scatter (Python, ao.staged._transform), which is not device code and is not timed; and compilation. So a row is the device cost of one J_p for a molecule whose index data is already resident, read back to the host ready for eq. 20 -- not a cold start and not a whole SCF iteration.
header.gate: #146: every row's raw carries build:gpu_util_before, build:gpu_util_after, build:gpu_busy_max, build:cpu_busy_permille_before, build:gate_discarded_phases. A cell's timing phase is one process run of the checked binary (warm-up plus repeats) between gate.wait_quiet (card at most build:gpu_busy_max percent busy by its own SMI, CPU at most gate.BUSY_MAX) and gate.after_reading; a phase whose after-reading was non-idle or unknown is DISCARDED and retaken, and counted in build:gate_discarded_phases. A contended timing is a different experiment, not a noisy one: nothing from a discarded phase is in a row, and the loader refuses a row whose card state is unknown or over the threshold.
header.checked: The timed binary is the checked binary: before timing, each cell's driver is run in its correctness mode and its J asserted against the launch oracle (launch.walk) and the libcint fixture (test/test_j_launched_ondevice.py's tolerances), and every timed process's first and last J_p must agree with it within the fp64-atomic run-to-run bound.
header.plan: raw 'build:classes', 'build:kernels' (batch-kernel launches per build), 'build:bra_classes', 'build:ket_classes', 'build:n_pairs' and 'build:n_skipped' (the launch oracle's screen count on the same plan: the (bra, ket) record pairs the kernel's break skips), and 'build:refused' (classes built at 1 batch because the plan refused the asked count).
header.not_compared: Report, do not compare: nothing here is compared against [JEngine]'s A100 build times, nor across vendors (gfx1200 rate-limits fp64), nor against kernels.json's synthetic-input class timings.
header.rerun: env FJ_LAUNCH_WALLCLOCK_STORE=data/measured/builds.json devtools/kernel-tier.sh --backend <cuda|hip> -- -n 0 -s -k build_wallclock (alone; one session per card).
